name: Beth Horon
overview: Beth Horon refers to two ancient Canaanite cities, the upper and nether Bethhoron, which held strategic importance in Israel's conquest of the land. Scripture records a significant victory near these cities when Joshua led Israel to defeat the Amorites, with the LORD intervening by casting down hailstones upon their fleeing enemies (Joshua 10:10-11). Additionally, Beth Horon is noted in the delineation of tribal borders, marking the inheritance boundaries of Ephraim and reflecting territorial shifts, including areas once held by Judah but later taken by the ten tribes (Joshua 16:3, 16:5; 18:13). These references underscore Beth Horon's role both as a military landmark and a marker of tribal inheritance in the unfolding history of Israel.
